chunks: There was just one blast, and they were extinguished.
ai.seo_question: What does the 'single blast' signify in Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the absolute sovereignty of God's command, where a single 'Sahqa' (blast) instantly reduces the powerful to nothingness, illustrating the brevity of worldly life compared to the eternal reality of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder of the suddenness of death and resurrection, urging believers to prepare spiritually while the opportunity remains. The imagery underscores the futility of worldly pride when confronted with the divine decree.
